title: Centered toric tower lifts and their centered identifications
statement: Let $M$ be a fine monoscheme, let $T=(X_i,J_i,b_i)_{0\leq i<n}$ be an ordered normalized scheme blowup tower, and let $e_0:X_0\simeq\mathbf Q[M]$ be specified, using [def-trf-monoscheme-toric-realization] and the composites to the initial scheme from [def-per-normalized-tower-descent-data]. Say that $T$ has equivariant toric centers if, for every original component torus and each $i<n$, its action lifts over $X_i\to X_0\to\mathbf Q[M]$ and the pullback of the actual ideal $J_i$ by that lift equals its pullback by projection. Action domains and equivariant comparisons are those of [def-trf-toric-action-comparison]. A centered toric tower lift consists of an ordered saturated monoscheme blowup tower $N$, an equality $N_0=M$, torsion-freeness of every $N_i$, and isomorphisms $\alpha_i:\mathbf Q[N_i]\simeq X_i$. Require that $\alpha_0e_0$ is the map induced by $N_0=M$, that $\mathbf Q[I_i]=\alpha_i^*J_i$, and that the canonical monomial arrow realizations commute with $b_i$ and the $\alpha_i$. Require also that every $\alpha_i$ is a toric comparison over the original realization. Given two such lifts $L,L'$, a centered identification is a family of isomorphisms $e_i:N_i\simeq N'_i$ of sheafed monoidal spaces fixing the specified base, commuting with all arrows, pulling $I'_i$ back to $I_i$, and whose hom maps are local monoscheme maps realizing to $\alpha_i(\alpha'_i)^{-1}$. This defines data and predicates only, and asserts neither their existence nor their uniqueness.

source.place: Exposé VIII, 3.2.14--3.2.20, pp.105--106, with the saturated charts of 3.1.19--3.1.24, pp.101--102.
